# awask

> Your agent asks you a question — and acts on your answer.

A decision buried in terminal prose is a stream event — it scrolls past, and the agent either stalls waiting for someone who is not reading, or guesses and does days of the wrong work. Every agent framework can print a question; almost none can carry the ANSWER back into the run that asked it, so the human is a bottleneck exactly when they are least able to be one.

## Install

```
pip install awask
```

## Use it in 30 seconds

Ask a human a question from a script, and keep working on their answer.

## Composes with

- [awdk](https://aitherium.github.io/awdk/) — Build AI agent fleets — 3 lines, any backend, local or cloud.
- [awrelay](https://aitherium.github.io/awrelay/) — Portable agent messaging — findings, alerts, coordination.
- [awmail](https://aitherium.github.io/awmail/) — Give an agent an email address — send, and actually receive.
- [awsh](https://aitherium.github.io/awsh/) — Your terminal answers you -- type a question where a command would go.
- [awnest](https://aitherium.github.io/awnest/) — Prove there is a human before you let them into the nest.
- [awrise](https://aitherium.github.io/awrise/) — Wake an agent on a schedule, let it do one thing, and put it back to sleep.
